items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: I would work about three nights a week with Al Streeman

ctx.x: As far as I know. Right, he's been here so long, I just assume he's still there.

He was assistant band director when Morrissey was band director. Now I think Ted is band director. And next to Ted is Al Streeman at the piano. This is a photograph of the Al Streeman dance orchestra. And that was taken in 1955, and I think it's in a Roosevelt Hotel in the Grand Ballroom. Someone shot that picture. Whenever a professional photographer shoots a picture, I usually try to get a copy of it just for my recording.
So you'd come back and play a spot with him, even though you would be playing with George Girard.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Al Estraticos used to play on the Jung roof, I think. [INTERVIEWEE] Right.

ctx.x: No. This one holding up the bass, the string bass, is Eddie Dusan. He's a practicing attorney today. And the fellow right next to him is Irvin Dusan, who today is president of Columbia Homestead and hasn't played music in a number of years.
Al Estraticos used to play on the Jung roof, I think.

items.title: Bob Coquille Interview, 1978-11-15
items.q: I think around 1939 I was with Al Streeman.

ctx.x: A drummer. Did you tell me or not?

No, I can't recall who was on drums because we went through one or two drummers too. Yeah, well. Drummers and, uh, drummers I can't recall. Chatelaine was on trombone. Were you in the union then? Oh no, this is way before the union. We never joined the union until, uh, I think around 1939 I was with Al Streeman.
